fallback.text: The triangle A(0, 0), B(6, 0), C(2, 4) has its circumcentre at O(3, 1), its centroid at G(8/3, 4/3), its orthocentre at H(2, 2) and its nine-point centre at N(2.5, 1.5), the midpoint of OH. All four lie on the Euler line x + y = 4, and HG is exactly twice GO (Euler 1767). The line passes through the vertex C only when the triangle is isosceles with CA = CB (C straight above the midpoint of AB, x = 3) or right-angled at C, where H falls on C itself; for an equilateral triangle all the centres coincide and there is no Euler line. The picture shows the triangle with its circumcircle, its nine-point circle (half the radius) and the Euler line.
